answer: A market that admits every new key on sight lets one operator flood it with aliases. Admission instead requires a relic path: the recruit collects unpaid sponsorships that spiral through already-settled members, each locking a sliver of coin for one cooling epoch. Cost is split — a fee from the recruit plus slash risk on every sponsor if the new key later fails a random audit. Peers recompute those signed edges in an ocean of prior settlements and check that each path is unique. It fails if one sponsor can endorse a bundle, so each relic is single-use, and a slash also burns that path.
